title: A Passage for the Monsoon
premise: Coral Dravenmoor, a desert ranger chasing a thief who stole his family's compass, follows the trail to a drowned coast where the retreating tide exposes a sea cave said to hold the inheritance of a disgraced shipping dynasty. Trapped by the early monsoon, Coral shelters in the cave with Sable Quill, a smuggler's daughter who knows its secrets and claims the legacy is hers by blood. As floodwaters rise and a corrupt magistrate's men close in to seize the cave's contents, Coral must choose between recovering what was stolen from him and helping Sable claim justice the law will never grant. In the climax they outlast the storm by scuttling the magistrate's ship in the flooded cavern, and Coral ends the monsoon not with the compass repaid but with a new debt freely given — belonging found where he expected only nothing.
about_author: Casper Thornbury is the pen name of a former coastal surveyor who spent a decade mapping tide caves along forgotten trade routes before turning to fiction. He writes adventure novels about people stranded between debts and horizons.

chapters.title: Nothing to Track Across
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. On the empty salt flats, Coral tracks the thief Vess Marrow by the compass needle's wrongness, establishing his debt: the compass was pawned to save his brother, and he swore to bring it home. Beat: lonely determination sharpened into obsession.

chapters.title: The Town That Sold Its Harbor
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. He reaches Grayharbor, a dying port where everyone lies about Vess but one dockhand mentions the tide caves. Coral learns the magistrate Tolliver has posted rewards for 'unclaimed salvage.' Beat: unease — the law here is for sale.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gives Back
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. At low tide the sea withdraws impossibly far, revealing the mouth of the Monsoon Cave. Coral enters against every ranger instinct and finds fresh bootprints — Vess's. Beat: awe curdling into dread as the water begins returning early.

chapters.title: A Stranger With a Boat
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable Quill rows into the cave on her leaking skiff, catches Coral mid-theft of her mooring line, and recognizes the compass instantly — she's been hunting Vess too. Beat: wary alliance struck over mutual hatred of the same man.

chapters.title: The Dynasties' Ledger
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Deep in the cave, Sable shows Coral the sealed strongroom of the Quill shipping dynasty: ledgers proving Tolliver's grandfather stole the fleet through forged debts. Her inheritance is paper proof, not gold. Beat: hope that feels fragile as glass.

chapters.title: Vess Marrow Explains Himself
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Cornered in an upper gallery, Vess reveals he stole the compass because it's a key — it aligns with a hidden channel through the reef, the only escape route when the monsoon seals the coast. Beat: the thief becomes necessary.

chapters.title: First Rain
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The monsoon arrives weeks early; rain hammers the coast and the cave begins flooding from below. The three are trapped together, and Coral's boat — borrowed, already leaking — becomes their only vessel. Beat: claustrophobic dread.

chapters.title: Bailing Water, Bailing Truths
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. While bailing the skiff, Sable tells how Tolliver hanged her father on a salvage charge. Coral admits his brother died waiting on the pawned compass money. Beat: two strangers' griefs interlock like gears.

chapters.title: Tolliver's Lanterns
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Through the cave mouth they spy Tolliver's men camped at the cliff top, waiting for the storm to pass so they can dynamite the cave open. Beat: the clock starts ticking louder than the rain.

chapters.title: The Compass Points Down
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Vess demonstrates the compass trick: held level in the flooded lower gallery, it swings toward a submerged passage. But using it means diving into black water during a storm surge. Beat: temptation versus terror.

chapters.title: A Debt Reconsidered
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral realizes taking the compass and swimming out alone would satisfy his oath — and abandon Sable to Tolliver. He spends a sleepless night deciding what a debt actually owes. Beat: the moral hinge of the book.

chapters.title: The Drowned Gallery
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Together they dive the submerged passage and find the dynasty's true vault: not treasure but the original deeds and a fleet charter that legally restores everything. Sable weeps in the dark. Beat: justice made tangible.

chapters.title: Betrayal at Low Ebb
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Vess steals the compass and the charter copy, intending to sell both to Tolliver, and takes the skiff's patch kit. Beat: bitter confirmation of Coral's old cynicism — and Sable's fury.

chapters.title: Rising Water, Falling Men
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The spring tide plus storm surge floods the main gallery; Tolliver's crew, impatient, enters the cave by rope and loses two men to the rising water. Coral saves one. Beat: mercy offered to an enemy's man.

chapters.title: The Rescued Man's Testimony
chapters.summary: Rescued sailor Brann's POV. Grateful and disgusted by Tolliver, Brann reveals the magistrate plans to blow the cave tonight with everyone inside, then report the 'salvage' destroyed. Beat: stakes become mortal and immediate.

chapters.title: Improvised Armada
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. They repair the skiff with sailcloth, pitch, and Brann's help, and plan to ride the surge out through the reef channel — if the compass can be recovered from Vess before Tolliver pays him. Beat: desperate ingenuity.

chapters.title: Where Thieves Trade
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral intercepts Vess at the half-drowned exchange point, and instead of fighting, offers him a share and a name cleared of the theft — the thing Vess actually wanted all along. Beat: the antagonist turns ally through dignity, not defeat.

chapters.title: Powder in the Dark
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Tolliver's sappers enter to set charges; Vess misleads them into rigging the powder below their own anchored patrol boat while Coral and Sable move the charter documents to the skiff. Beat: tension wound to snapping.

chapters.title: The Surge Takes All
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Climax. At peak surge they run the reef channel by compass light as the charges detonate, sinking Tolliver's patrol boat and sealing the cave behind them. Tolliver survives but loses his men, his evidence, and his cover story. Beat: cathartic, terrifying release.

chapters.title: Aftermath in Gray Light
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Storm-wracked Grayharbor wakes to find the charter nailed to the customs house door and Brann testifying freely. Tolliver is arrested by his own garrison. Beat: justice arriving outside any courtroom.

chapters.title: Settling Accounts
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral gives the compass to Sable — it belongs to the channel, to her legacy — and accepts that some debts are paid by handing forward, not back. Vess sails north with a clean slate and a share. Beat: quiet, earned peace.

chapters.title: A Passage for the Monsoon
chapters.summary: Shared POV, closing pages. Months later, Coral stays on as warden of the reopened harbor route, guiding ships through the channel each monsoon. Sable's fleet returns under honest colors. Beat: belonging chosen, not inherited — the ranger who tracked across nothing finally has somewhere to stand.
